string-array.name: help_ecu_voltage
string-array.item: System voltage as measured by the engine ECU at its own power supply.

On the CTS, charging is controlled by GM RVC (Regulated Voltage Control): alternator voltage changes with battery charge and temperature. So a \"floating\" voltage while driving is normal. In fuel economy mode (battery charged, low current) the alternator holds no more than 12.9 V — also normal, not \"not charging\".

Because of RVC, a single low reading means nothing. It\'s a concern if the voltage stays low for a long time and there is also a charging warning on the cluster or power-related codes in the modules (e.g. P0562 — system voltage low).

string-array.name: help_adapter_voltage
string-array.item: Voltage at pin 16 of the OBD port, measured by the adapter itself.
Should be close to \"Voltage (ECU)\": slightly lower because of the wiring to the port.
Very different from the ECU value — the OBD port, ground or the diagnostic circuit fuse. On cheap ELM327 clones the measurement itself can be inaccurate — go by the ECU value.

string-array.name: help_ambient
string-array.item: Outside air temperature from the car\'s sensor, reported by the engine ECU.
Close to actual while driving. When stopped or after a drive it may read high: the sensor is heated by the engine and the road.
Shows −40 °C — usually an open sensor circuit: that\'s the bottom of the scale.

string-array.name: help_baro
string-array.item: Atmospheric pressure as reported by the ECU.
About 101 kPa at sea level, dropping by roughly 1.2 kPa per 100 m of altitude. Weather changes it slightly too.
Very different from what you\'d expect at your altitude — suspect the sensor. The mixture calculation depends on this value.
